Quick answers:
- RTO targets: 15 minutes (control plane), 30 seconds–5 minutes for model token stream recovery depending on model variant and KV cache priming strategy; see attached summary.
- RPO targets: near-zero for routed customer metadata and session tokens; up to 15 minutes for non-critical cache layers depending on configuration.

- Test cadence: quarterly full failover drills for Dedicated customers, semi-annual for hosted customers; ad-hoc rehearsals per contract.

Alex / Marissa —

Attaching the technical artifacts requested. Below are the key details pulled from the attachments for quick review.

RTO / RPO by service (typical configuration, default redwood-hosted):
- API control plane (management operations): RTO 15 minutes, RPO near-zero (replicated config store)
- Text generation (low-latency streaming): RTO 60s–3m depending on sequence warmup; RPO near-zero for customer-auth and routing metadata; model state (KV cache) RPO up to 10–15 minutes if not persisted between sessions
- Embeddings / batch workloads: RTO 5–15 minutes (cold-start depends on batch scheduling); RPO 15 minutes (workload retries are standard)
- Dedicated pools (reserved): target RTO 5–10 minutes with pre-warmed instances; RPO near-zero when replication enabled

Multi-region failover sequence (high-level):
1) Detection and circuit breaker: automated detection via latency/error thresholds triggers policy.
2) Traffic steering: Route-level weights adjusted by the router to redirect new sessions to healthy region; in-flight short sessions are allowed to complete with graceful fallback.
3) KV cache rehydration: We perform prefix cache priming from persistent checkpoints where configured; otherwise soft-warm strategy with prioritized rehydration for active customers.
4) Model variant fallback: If a quantized/compatible variant is required to preserve throughput in constrained regions, the platform will automatically switch with signalized headers for transparency.
5) Post-failover reconciliation: background syncing of telemetry, telemetry-based validation, and a post-mortem runbook to capture timeline and customer impact.

Test cadence and evidence:
- We run scheduled rehearsal drills: quarterly for Dedicated and annual full cross-region drills for hosted customers; last verified full cross-region drill for hosted control plane: 2026-06-21 (drill id: DRILL-20260621-HOSTED).
- Included evidence: runbook excerpt (runbook-switchover-snippet.txt), RTO/RPO matrix (rto-rpo-matrix.csv), and a redacted packet of post-drill logs in redwood-bcp-evidence.zip.

Security & controls: all cross-region data transfers use TLS 1.3; keys in KMS with restricted access; audit logs retained per contract (default 90 days, enterprise packages extended).

Notes on test impact: During a full cross-region failover we may see increased token latency for a short window (seconds to low minutes) while caches are rehydrated. We aim to keep model output consistency via prioritized cache priming for high-volume routes.

Attachments: runbook-switchover-snippet.txt (text), rto-rpo-matrix.csv (csv), redwood-bcp-evidence.zip (zip)

--
